event.centerRule: The first Passover remains the central Event. Later laws, observances, Gospel feasts, and apostolic arguments remain attached to their own Scripture sources rather than being treated as repetitions of one scene or combined into an unreported chronology.

characterAnchors.label: The LORD
characterAnchors.note: Speaks the first instructions, passes through Egypt, strikes the firstborn, spares marked houses, brings Israel out, and remains the named recipient of later observance.

characterAnchors.label: Moses
characterAnchors.note: Receives and transmits the first instructions, directs the elders, explains recurring memory, hears participation questions, and writes the journey record.

characterAnchors.label: Aaron
characterAnchors.note: Receives the first words with Moses and stands with him through the night, release, ordinance, and later wilderness question.

characterAnchors.label: Israelite households
characterAnchors.note: Select, prepare, eat, mark doors, remain inside, depart, remember, and transmit the service through later generations.

characterAnchors.label: Pharaoh and the Egyptians
characterAnchors.note: Receive the announced judgment, experience the midnight deaths and cry, summon Israel, press the departure, and remain present in later memory.

characterAnchors.label: Children and later generations
characterAnchors.note: Are anticipated as questioners whose answers connect recurring practice with what happened in Egypt.

characterAnchors.label: Resident foreigners
characterAnchors.note: Appear in participation rulings that preserve both boundaries and one shared statute.

characterAnchors.label: Priests and Levites
characterAnchors.note: Prepare, purify, sacrifice, distribute, sing, bless, and serve in wilderness, royal, and return observances.

characterAnchors.label: Hezekiah
characterAnchors.note: Calls Israel and Judah to a second-month Passover, prays for irregular participants, and shares in the extended celebration.

characterAnchors.label: Josiah
characterAnchors.note: Commands Passover from the covenant book and coordinates the feast preserved in Kings, Chronicles, and 1 Esdras.

characterAnchors.label: Jesus
characterAnchors.note: Travels to Passover, speaks and acts in feast settings, prepares or attends final-table scenes, and is placed by John within Preparation Day and unbroken-bone witness.

characterAnchors.label: Disciples and apostles
characterAnchors.note: Prepare meals, ask and answer at the table, remember earlier words, receive bread and cup, and appear in distinct Gospel Passover sequences.

characterAnchors.label: Judas
characterAnchors.note: Objects within an anointing account, negotiates delivery, remains at distinct final-table scenes, and departs into the night in John.

characterAnchors.label: Pilate
characterAnchors.note: Questions Jesus across the Gospel hearings, invokes the feast-release custom, and delivers Jesus under crowd and political pressure.

event.throughline: A final plague is announced; households prepare a marked meal; Egypt’s firstborn die and Israel departs; the night becomes recurring food, speech, calendar, participation, and place; later generations keep, restore, retell, and interpret Passover in changing settings.

topic.orientation: Enter Passover through the announced firstborn night, household preparation, release, departure, memorial, and participation. Then inspect its place in Israel’s calendar, wilderness and land observances, royal and return celebrations, distinct Gospel feast approaches, tables, hearings, Preparation Day scenes, and explicit apostolic reuse.

passages.contextLine: The night approaches · antecedent
passages.excerpt: You shall tell Pharaoh, ‘The LORD says, Israel is my son, my firstborn,
passages.observation: Moses is told to identify Israel as the LORD’s son and firstborn, demand release for service, and warn that Pharaoh’s refusal will be answered at his own firstborn son.
passages.title: Israel is named firstborn before Pharaoh is warned

passages.contextLine: The night approaches · setup
passages.excerpt: The LORD said to Moses, “I will bring yet one more plague on Pharaoh, and on Egypt; afterwards he will let you go. When he lets you go, he will surely thrust you out altogether.
passages.observation: The LORD announces one final plague, Moses describes the death of Egypt’s firstborn at midnight, and departure is expected to follow.
passages.title: One more plague is announced before departure

passages.contextLine: The first Passover night · core
passages.excerpt: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
passages.observation: A new month is marked; households select an unblemished animal, eat in haste, place blood on their doors, and await the LORD’s passage through Egypt.
passages.title: A household meal, marked doors, and a night of judgment

passages.contextLine: Memory, participation, and firstborn · aftermath
passages.excerpt: This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall keep it as a feast to the LORD. You shall keep it as a feast throughout your generations by an ordinance forever.
passages.observation: Before the night is narrated, the day is appointed as a memorial feast with seven days of unleavened bread and two holy convocations.
passages.title: The first day becomes a recurring memorial

passages.contextLine: The first Passover night · core
passages.excerpt: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said to them, “Draw out, and take lambs according to your families, and kill the Passover.
passages.observation: Moses tells the elders to kill the Passover, apply blood with hyssop, remain inside, preserve the ordinance, and answer children who ask about the service.
passages.title: Elders carry the command to Israel’s doorways

passages.contextLine: The first Passover night · core
passages.excerpt: At midnight, the LORD struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon,…
passages.observation: At midnight Egypt’s firstborn die, a great cry rises, Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron, and the Egyptians press Israel to leave with dough and received goods.
passages.title: Midnight grief becomes urgent release

passages.contextLine: The first Passover night · aftermath
passages.excerpt: The children of Israel traveled from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot who were men, in addition to children.
passages.observation: Israel travels from Rameses to Succoth with a mixed multitude; unleavened dough, the long sojourn, and a night to be observed accompany the departure.
passages.title: The people depart and the night is kept in memory

passages.contextLine: Memory, participation, and firstborn · aftermath
passages.excerpt: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the ordinance of the Passover. No foreigner shall eat of it,
passages.observation: The ordinance names who may eat, circumcision for a resident foreigner, one-house handling, unbroken bones, the whole congregation, and one law.
passages.title: One-house boundaries and one law govern participation

passages.contextLine: Memory, participation, and firstborn · aftermath
passages.excerpt: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
passages.observation: Firstborn consecration, unleavened bread, the promised land, a child-directed explanation, embodied signs, and yearly observance preserve the exodus day.
passages.title: Departure becomes speech, sign, and yearly practice

passages.contextLine: Memory, participation, and firstborn · aftermath
passages.excerpt: “It shall be, when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to your fathers, and will give it to you,
passages.observation: In the promised land, firstborn animals and sons are set apart or redeemed, and a child’s question is answered by recalling Pharaoh’s refusal and the firstborn deaths.
passages.title: Firstborn redemption answers a future child’s question

passages.contextLine: Passover in Israel’s calendar · consequence
passages.excerpt: “You shall observe a feast to me three times a year.
passages.observation: The feast in Abib is placed beside harvest and ingathering, with appearance before God and rules about blood, leaven, and what remains overnight.
passages.title: Unleavened bread enters the three annual feasts

passages.contextLine: Passover in Israel’s calendar · consequence
passages.excerpt: “You shall keep the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib; for in the month Abib you…
passages.observation: The feast in Abib is restated alongside firstborn ownership, redemption, Sabbath, other feasts, appearing before God, blood, leaven, and the overnight boundary.
passages.title: Feast, firstborn, rest, appearance, and sacrifice gather together

passages.contextLine: Passover in Israel’s calendar · consequence
passages.excerpt: “‘These are the set feasts of the LORD, even holy convocations, which you shall proclaim in their appointed season.
passages.observation: The appointed calendar places Passover on the fourteenth evening and the Feast of Unleavened Bread on the fifteenth, bounded by holy convocations and offerings.
passages.title: Passover opens a seven-day appointed feast

passages.contextLine: Passover in Israel’s calendar · consequence
passages.excerpt: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
passages.observation: In the second year after leaving Egypt, Israel keeps the Passover at Sinai on its appointed date according to the commanded statutes.
passages.title: Israel keeps Passover in the wilderness

passages.contextLine: Passover in Israel’s calendar · consequence
passages.excerpt: There were certain men who were unclean because of the dead body of a man, so that they could not keep the Passover on that day, and they came before Moses and Aaron on that day.
passages.observation: Men excluded by corpse impurity bring their question to Moses; a second-month provision addresses impurity and travel while preserving meal rules, obligation, and one statute for the foreigner.
passages.title: A delayed Passover answers impurity and distance

passages.excerpt: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

passages.contextLine: The night remembered in later Scripture · later memory
passages.excerpt: Thus you shall separate the Levites from among the children of Israel, and the Levites shall be mine.
passages.observation: The Levites are separated and given for sanctuary service in place of Israel’s firstborn, with the substitution again tied to the day Egypt’s firstborn were struck.

passages.excerpt: “‘In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the LORD’s Passover.
passages.observation: Passover and the following feast are dated, and daily burnt, meal, drink, and sin offerings are specified alongside convocations and rest.
passages.title: Daily offerings accompany the seven feast days

passages.contextLine: The night remembered in later Scripture · later memory
passages.excerpt: These are the journeys of the children of Israel, when they went out of the land of Egypt by their armies under the hand of Moses and Aaron.
passages.observation: The written itinerary begins at Rameses on the day after Passover while Egyptians bury their firstborn and judgment on Egypt’s gods is recalled.
passages.phase: The night remembered in later Scripture
passages.title: The journey list begins the day after Passover

passages.contextLine: Passover in Israel’s calendar · consequence
passages.excerpt: Observe the month of Abib, and keep the Passover to the LORD your God; for in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
passages.observation: The observance in Abib recalls the night departure, names sacrifice at the chosen place, calls unleavened bread the bread of affliction, and ends with assembly and rest.
passages.title: Passover is kept at the chosen place

passages.contextLine: Passover in the land and after return · consequence
passages.excerpt: The children of Israel encamped in Gilgal. They kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month at evening in the plains of Jericho.
passages.observation: At Gilgal Israel keeps Passover, eats produce of the land the next day, and no longer receives manna.

passages.contextLine: Passover in the land and after return · consequence
passages.excerpt: The king commanded all the people, saying, “Keep the Passover to the LORD your God, as it is written in this book of the covenant.”
passages.observation: Josiah orders the people to keep Passover as written, and the narrator marks the eighteenth-year observance in Jerusalem as unlike those since the judges.
passages.phase: Passover in the land and after return
passages.title: Josiah commands Passover from the covenant book

passages.contextLine: Passover in the land and after return · consequence
passages.excerpt: Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the LORD’s house at Jerusalem, to keep the Passover to the LORD,…
passages.observation: Letters travel through Israel and Judah inviting people to Jerusalem in the second month; the appeal calls for return, receives mockery, and also draws a humbled remnant.

passages.title: Hezekiah calls a divided people to a second-month Passover

passages.contextLine: Passover in the land and after return · consequence
passages.excerpt: Many people assembled at Jerusalem to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month, a very great assembly.
passages.observation: A large assembly removes altars, keeps Passover despite incomplete purification, receives Hezekiah’s prayer, continues in praise, and chooses another seven days.
passages.phase: Passover in the land and after return
passages.title: Prayer, healing, praise, and extended joy fill the feast

passages.contextLine: Passover in the land and after return · consequence
passages.excerpt: Josiah kept a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem. They killed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
passages.observation: Josiah, priests, Levites, leaders, singers, and gatekeepers prepare offerings and service by written instructions, and the narrator compares the feast with the days of Samuel.
passages.phase: Passover in the land and after return
passages.title: Josiah orders a Passover of coordinated service
